payload.text:
"¡Eh, amigo! Paco here — my brother Nando, don't mind him, he's counting."
"I'm counting your lucky day! Look — Huevos Rotos, straight from the case, barely touched the light."
"Four P. Four! We leave at sundown, so—"
"—so decide fast, guapo. Four P, and it's yours."
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Thirty in the world — sí, I know the number better than you, señor. But eighty is a fantasy. Sixty-four P, and said with affection for El Retiro. I do not enjoy repeating myself.

"¡Guapo, guapo! You flatter like a poet, but Nando's ears only hear numbers—"

"—and the number sings four. Four P, amigo. Same as before, same as always, because it's already a regalo."

"Sundown's coming. Say sí, take the Huevos Rotos, and we all walk away smiling."
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

Señor, your efforts are charming, but seventy-six remains a fantasy. Sixty-six P — and that is affection speaking, not arithmetic. The Ángel would rest in my safe tonight, among its equals. Decide, por favor; I dislike repeating myself.

"¡Nueve! Nando, did you hear — he's singing nine at us."

"I heard, hermano, and my heart stays at four. Four P, guapo, same beautiful number as the first time. We don't move, we only pack."

"Sun's dropping, amigo. Four P, and the Huevos Rotos go home with you."
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

"—and we stay planted. Four P, guapo. That's our last word, final, no more songs."

"Say sí now, or we close the suitcase and walk. Four P, Huevos Rotos, done. Sundown doesn't wait, and neither do we."

You again. Silver pack, one eighty-eight. That is the number. Take it or walk.
Your manners honour you, señor. Sixty-nine P — and that is my last word. One peseta separates us, so do not test me further. Accept now, or I close my safe and we part politely.

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, show him the good one — sí, Mercado de la Cebada, the jewel of the case! My tía sold oranges there, true story. For you, because your face is honest, cuatro P. Four! But hurry, hombre, we pack up soon.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.

Buenas tardes. I am afraid not — commons hold no interest for me, señor. My albums require something finer. Bring me uncommons, or better, from Salamanca or El Retiro, and we shall have a proper conversation.

¡Once! Paco, ¿oíste? He wants to pay us eleven — ¡qué corazón! But no, hombre, we are honest men, we said cuatro P and cuatro P it stays. Four, amigo. Take it quick, the case closes in two minutes and the train does not wait.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P.

¡Nueve! Paco, this man wants to ruin us with generosity! No, no, amigo — cinco P, five, that is our word and we never break it. The case is closing, the train whistles, Nando is already walking. Cinco P, hombre, take it now!

¡Buenas, cariño! Qué alegría verte. ¿Has comido ya? Mira, la Estación de Chamberí te la dejo en 29 primas, y te completa la página bonita. La chulapa dorada... me suena, sí. El Chato, mi vecino de al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche. Pregúntale, hijo.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? This one, the Escaparate de Serrano, very pretty card — twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always.

Ay, hijo, qué cosas más bonitas me dices. Mira, te la dejo en 26 primas y tan amigos, ¿eh? Y un consejo, cariño: la página entera vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. Trae tus repetidas y cámbialas, que siempre hay alguien a quien le faltan.

¡Cinco! Paco, he said cinco — ¡trato hecho! Take it, amigo, the Mercado de la Cebada is yours, wrapped and gone. A pleasure, de verdad. Nando, close the case, the train is whistling! ¡Adiós, hombre, and enjoy it!

Ay, cocido de tres vuelcos! Just like my mother made, hijo — the soup first, always. You remembered, that warms me. Take it, the Escaparate de Serrano, twelve P, and I put a little duplicate in your hand for free. Swap it, fill your page, cariño.

Ay, cariño, qué paciencia tienes tú conmigo. Mira, 24 primas y cerramos, ¿eh? Es una carta preciosa, y tu página queda completa. Y luego te pasas por El Chato a las nueve y media, que a él le gusta la gente que trata derecha. ¿Pero has comido ya, hijo?
